Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Jai Raj
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.

1. Heard Mr. Mahesh Chandra Tiwari, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mr. Jai Raj, the learned counsel representing first informant/opposite party-4.
2.
Perused the Court.

3. This application for bail has been filed by applicant Sanjay @ Sanju, seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 25 of 2023 under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Sections 5J (ii)/6 POCSO Act, Police Station-Jagdishpura, District- Agra during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: 4. At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. submits that notice of present bail application has been served upon first informant/opposite party-4 on 17.03.2023.

However, inspite of service of notice,
no one has put in appearance on behalf of first informant/opposite party-4 to oppose this application.

5. Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred on 13.01.2023, a delayed F.I.R. dated 14.01.2023 was lodged by first informant/opposite party-4 Rakesh (Father of the prosecurix) and was registered as Case Crime No. 25 of 2023 under Sections 363, 366, 120B I.P.C., Police Station-Jagdishpura, District- Agra
In the aforesaid F.I.R., three persons namely Sanjay (applicant herein), Smt. Kamla Devi and Vineeta have been nominated as named accused.
6. The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R. is to the effect that named accused have kidnapped the daughter of first informant namely X, aged about 14 years.
7. Subsequent to the aforesaid F.I.R., Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of aforesaid case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr.P.C.
The prosecutrix was recovered on 15.01.2023.
Thereafter the statement of prosecutrix was recorded by the Investigating Officer under Section 161 Cr.P.C, which is on record at page 19 of the paper book.
The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement, has not supported the F.I.R.
To the contrary she has stated that she herself accompanied the applicant out of her own free will.
Thereafter prosecutrix was requested for her internal medical examination but the same was denied by her.
The Medico Legal Report of the prosecutrix has been brought on record at page 13 of the paper book.
The USG test (Ultra Sound) of the prosecutrix was conducted.
The prosecutrix was reported to be in family way and the age of foetus was diagnosed to be nine weeks.
As per medical opinion, the age of the prosecutrix was determined to be 17 years.
Ultimately, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. copy of which is on record at page 25 of the paper book.
In her aforesaid statement, the prosecutrix has rejoined her previous statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. referred to above.
8. During course of investigation, Investigating Officer examined the first informant and other witnesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C., who have substantially supported the F.I.R.

On the basis of above and other material collected by Investigating Officer during the course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that complicity of applicant is fully established in the crime in question.

He accordingly submitted the charge-sheet dated 24.03.2023.
9.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that though the applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.

He submits that since the prosecutrix is an illiterate lady, therefore there is no material regarding her schooling as such there is no educational record with regard to her date of birth on the basis of which her age could be determined.
Investigating Officer has not collected any other material in connivance with the provisions contained in Section 94 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015.

sentences.text: As such, age of the prosecutrix has to be considered in the light of the medical opinion on record.
As per medical opinion, the prosecutrix is 17 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Referring to the statements of the prosecutrix as recorded under Sections 161/164 Cr.P.C., he submit that the prosecutrix is a willing and consenting party.
Neither the prosecutrix has been kidnapped nor she has been adducted but she came to the applicant out of her own free will.
As such, no offence under Section as complained of can be said to have been committed by the applicant.
11. Even otherwise applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as he has no criminal history except the present one.
Applicant is in custody since 30.01.2023.
As such he has undergone more than eight and a half months of incarceration.

The police report (charge-sheet) in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted, therefore, the entire evidence sought to relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallised.
Upto this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
He therefore submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
12. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. for State and the learned counsel representing first informant have opposed the prayer for bail.
They submit that since the applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.

He has then invited the attention of the Court to the supplementary medico legal report of the prosecutrix and as per the radiological report, the prosecutrix was reported to be in family way and the age of the foetus was diagonised to be nine weeks.
As such, the provisions contained in Sections 5 J (ii)/ 6 of POSCO are clearly attracted.
against applicant.
Upto this stage, learned counsel for applicant has been unable to dislodge the said fact.
Considering the nature of offence and the age of the prosecutrix, they submit that no sympathy be shown by this court in favour of applicant.
13. When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

14. Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon consideration of material on record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence, accusations made as well as complicity of applicant coupled with the fact that as per supplementary medico legal report, the prosecutrix is reported to be in family way and the age of the foetus has been determined to be nine weeks, the said fact could not be dislodged by the learned counsel for applicant, there is nothing on record to show that the prosecutrix and applicant have solemnized marriage, therefore irrespective of the submissions urged by learned counsel for applicant in support of this applicant for bail but without making any comments on the merits of the case this Court finds that no good ground has been made out to enlarge the applicant on bail.
15. As a result, bail application of applicant fails and is liable to be rejected.
16. It is accordingly rejected.
